blurb: An ascetic path of ahimsa — nonviolence toward every living being — taught by a line of Tirthankaras and preserved by monks, nuns, and a devoted lay community.

events.description: Jain tradition remembers Parshvanatha teaching four vows centuries before Mahavira. Many historians accept him as a real ascetic of roughly the 8th–7th century BCE, though the evidence is thin.
events.title: Parshvanatha, the 23rd Tirthankara

events.description: Vardhamana Mahavira renounces royal life, attains omniscience (kevala), and organizes monks, nuns, and lay followers around ahimsa — nonviolence toward every living being. Traditional dates 599–527 BCE; many scholars place him in the 5th century BCE.
events.title: Life of Mahavira

events.description: By tradition, after a famine, Jain elders at Pataliputra gather to preserve the scriptures — an early step toward a canon, and (in the Digambara telling) the point after which the original texts were lost.
events.title: Council of Pataliputra & the early canon

events.description: The one Sanskrit Jain text accepted by both major sects systematizes Jain metaphysics — soul, karma as subtle matter, bondage, and liberation through the three jewels: right faith, knowledge, and conduct.
events.title: Umasvati's Tattvartha Sutra

events.description: Over centuries the Jain community splits over monastic nudity, the authenticity of scriptures, and whether women can attain liberation directly — into 'sky-clad' Digambaras and 'white-clad' Shvetambaras.
events.title: The community divides: Digambara & Shvetambara

events.description: A council at Valabhi in Gujarat commits the Shvetambara canon (the Agamas) to writing — the form in which most early Jain scripture survives.
events.title: The Shvetambara canon written down at Valabhi

events.description: The 17-meter statue of Bahubali at Shravanabelagola, carved from a single rock under the Western Ganga dynasty, becomes Jainism's most famous pilgrimage monument — the ascetic ideal made colossal.
events.title: Gommateshwara consecrated

events.description: Jain teacher Virchand Gandhi addresses the 1893 World's Parliament of Religions; Mahatma Gandhi, mentored by the Jain scholar-monk Raychand, makes ahimsa a political force; Jain communities later flourish across East Africa, Britain, and North America.
events.title: Ahimsa goes global: Gandhi & the diaspora

name: Jainism
